entries.title: CTX mosaic, regional context (62.5 km across) centred on Jezero Crater
entries.institution: NASA/JPL/MSSS/The Murray Lab (Caltech); tiles hosted by Esri for NASA Solar System Treks
entries.license: Free use of the CTX beta01 mosaic for all purposes with credit (Murray Lab statement on the service page)
entries.acquisition_note: Mosaic of many CTX orbits (2006 onward); individual acquisition dates are not tracked in the beta01 mosaic.
entries.resolution_note: Tile pixel 81.4 m N-S (77.22 m E-W at this latitude); the underlying CTX mosaic is ~5 m/px, resampled for this zoom level.

bounds.source: WMTS/ArcGIS tile grid, zoom 9, rows 202-204, cols 731-733

entries.coverage_evidence: Bounds computed exactly from the WMTS tile grid at zoom 9; the candidate coordinate (18.4447, 77.4508) lies in the centre tile.
entries.relevance: Covers the whole ~59 km analysis footprint; the regional slope and relief statistics describe this area.
entries.appearance_note: Uncontrolled greyscale CTX mosaic (beta01): brightness varies between orbit strips and seams can be visible; lossy JPEG tiles.

entries.title: Perseverance and Mars 2020 Spacecraft Components on the Surface
entries.institution: JPL / NASA Image and Video Library
entries.license: NASA imagery: free to use for any purpose with credit (NASA Media Usage Guidelines)
entries.acquisition_note: Caption: image taken on Feb. 19, 2021, the day after landing.
entries.resolution_note: Ground sampling of this web-sized asset is not stated by the source.
entries.coverage_evidence: Caption states the rover sits at the centre of the sky-crane blast pattern; the candidate coordinate is the Perseverance touchdown point.
entries.relevance: The exact landing location seen from orbit, with the descent-stage debris, heat shield and parachute. Shows the terrain at the candidate point itself.
entries.appearance_note: HiRISE enhanced colour; relative contrast stretched to show hardware.

entries.title: A Possible Landing Site for the 2020 Mission: Jezero Crater
entries.institution: JPL / NASA Image and Video Library
entries.license: NASA imagery: free to use for any purpose with credit (NASA Media Usage Guidelines)
entries.acquisition_note: Acquisition date not stated on the product page; released 2015 during landing-site selection.
entries.resolution_note: Ground sampling of this web-sized asset is not stated by the source.
entries.coverage_evidence: Caption: 'a possible landing site for the 2020 mission: Jezero Crater' imaged to identify hazards within a landing ellipse; the exact offset of this scene from the final touchdown point is not stated.
entries.relevance: Landing-ellipse scale HiRISE view used in site selection; somewhere within the Jezero landing region, not necessarily the touchdown point.

entries.title: Mastcam-Z's First 360-Degree Panorama
entries.institution: JPL / NASA Image and Video Library
entries.license: NASA imagery: free to use for any purpose with credit (NASA Media Usage Guidelines)
entries.resolution_note: Ground sampling of this web-sized asset is not stated by the source.
entries.coverage_evidence: First 360-degree panorama from the rover at its landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing); the candidate coordinate is that touchdown point.
entries.relevance: What the ground looks like at the candidate point: the surface panorama from the landing site, with the crater rim on the horizon.
entries.appearance_note: Mastcam-Z colour balanced for Earth-like lighting; the horizon is tens of kilometres away.
